one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window: the September revenue report (~Oct 9-10) and Q3 2026 results plus Q4 guidance on Oct 15. July (~NT$467.6B) + August (NT$514.8B) revenue already total NT$982B, so September needs only ~NT$445-485B to hit the $44.6-45.8B guide at NT$32; a ~NT$490B September would put Q3 near $46B, above the top of the range. Consensus (Q3 ADR EPS $4.46, revenue NT$1,455B) already sits above guide midpoint, so a beat is largely expected; the swing factor is Q4 guidance and the gross margin trajectory as the steep N2 ramp dilutes 3-4pts. TSMC has a long record of beating its own guide, and estimate revisions are running 9 up / 0 down over 30 days, so I lean slightly positive (median ~$463, +0.8%) with spread at roughly the stock's monthly vol (40%/3.5 = 11.4%). The earnings print raises event risk, but I don't have an edge on direction beyond a small drift.

fair_value.method: Blend of 20x NTM EPS at Oct 2027 ($24.9 -> $498, weight 0.6) and a 5-year FCF DCF at 9.5% discount / 4% terminal ($426, weight 0.4) = ~$469 per ADR.

bear.story: AI capex digestion in 2027: hyperscaler or GPU-customer orders slow, N2 and overseas-fab dilution push gross margin toward 58-60%, FY2028 EPS growth stalls near $22, and the multiple compresses to ~14x. Includes a small tail for a Taiwan-strait shock or punitive tariffs.

base.story: 2026 closes ~+40% USD revenue growth as guided, 2027 EPS lands near the $21.9 consensus, and the market pays ~20x for ~$25 NTM EPS in Oct 2027 as N2/A16 ramps and CoWoS stays sold out.

bull.story: AI demand keeps beating ('stronger than what we said before'), price increases stick, N2 dilution fades faster, and FY2028 EPS reaches ~$28. With ~24x on that, the stock gets to ~$680.

thesis_break_reason: $330 equals ~15x the $21.93 FY2027 consensus, a trough-cycle multiple. Getting there would most likely require 2027 estimates to be cut (AI order pushouts from the top-2 customers, which were 36% of 2025 revenue) or a geopolitical/tariff repricing, not ordinary 40%-vol noise. It is also ~28% below spot and under the 52-week range midpoint.

key_uncertainties: How long AI accelerator demand lasts into 2027-28: TSMC's top two customers were 36% of 2025 revenue
Gross margin path: 3-4pt N2 dilution plus 2-4pt overseas-fab dilution against pricing power
Capex intensity: 'significantly higher' capex over the next 3 years could squeeze FCF
Geopolitics: Polymarket prices 13% for a China invasion of Taiwan by end-2027; tariffs/Section 232
Quality of reported EPS: Q2 2026 pre-tax income exceeded operating income by ~NT$96B (non-operating gains, likely incl. the VIS stake sale), flattering net margin to 55.6%
TWD/USD moves: guidance assumes NT$32; spot 31.93
reasoning: Primary documents show operations accelerating. Q2 2026 revenue was NT$1,270B (+36% YoY), operating margin 60.3% and diluted EPS NT$27.25 ($4.31/ADR) vs $3.89 consensus. Q3 guidance is $44.6-45.8B, and July+August revenue (NT$982B) already puts Q3 on track to beat the top end. FY2026 guidance was raised to 'slightly above 40%' USD growth and capex to $60-64B. The August board approved another $29.4B of appropriations and a JPY 282B Sony image-sensor JV, and management says capex over the next three years will be 'significantly higher'. Points the recaps skip: Q2 pre-tax income exceeded operating income by ~NT$96B, inflating the 55.6% net margin (the May 6-K on selling 8.1% of VIS is the likely contributor), so run-rate EPS is a bit below the headline. Q3 gross margin is guided down 1.7pt on N2 dilution. The top-two customer share rose to 36% in 2025 per the 20-F. Share count is flat at ~25.93B (dividend 6-K), so EPS growth is not buyback-driven. Consensus ADR EPS is $16.93 for FY26 and $21.93 for FY27, revised up 9/0 in 30 days. Valuation: 20x NTM EPS of $24.9 at Oct 2027 gives $498, and the FCF DCF gives $426 because heavy capex holds FCF to ~$14.5/ADR in 2027. The blend is ~$469, only ~2% above spot. The stock already prices most of the good news (20.9x FY27 consensus, +64% in a year), so the 12-month median is set modestly above spot (~$495-500), with a lognormal spread (sigma 0.31) close to the 40% realized vol, plus a 5% crash component (median ~$210) for Taiwan or tariff shocks. This is lighter than the 13% Polymarket invasion-by-end-2027 price because that market's window runs 3 months past the horizon and invasion is not the same as a full equity wipeout. Scenarios: 20% bear at $300, 55% base at $500, 25% bull at $680 (mean ~$505), consistent with the ladder: P(>=459) = 0.58, P(>=505) = 0.46, P(>=689) = 0.14. Research limits: the TSMC IR PDFs (management report, official transcript) were blocked by a JS challenge, so I used SEC 6-K copies and third-party transcripts. Twelve Data analyst price targets need a paid plan and were not used.
